title: Graph the solution set of an inequality and interpret it in context

questions.skill: Graph the solution set of an inequality and interpret it in context
questions.response: draw on the figure and write an answer
questions.prompt: A taxi charges $3 plus $2 per mile. Ty can spend at most $15. Solve 2m + 3 ≤ 15 for the miles m. Then graph the possible distances on the number line. (Distances cannot be negative.)
questions.prompt_markup:
A taxi charges $3 plus $2 per mile. Ty can spend at most $15.
Solve 2m + 3 ≤ 15 for the miles m. Then graph the possible distances on the number line. (Distances cannot be negative.)
questions.drawing_answer: A closed circle at 6 and the line shaded from 0 to 6 (a closed circle or the end of the shading at 0)
questions.grading_note: Grade both: the solution 0 ≤ m ≤ 6 (m ≤ 6 with distances not negative), and the graph from 0 to 6 with a closed circle at 6.

figure.description: Horizontal number line from 0 to 10, tick marks every 1. Nothing is marked; the student draws on it.

questions.skill: Graph the solution set of an inequality and interpret it in context
questions.response: draw on the figure and write an answer
questions.prompt: A freezer is at 2°C and cools 1.5°C each hour. Solve 2 - 1.5t < -4 to find when it is colder than -4°C. Then graph the solution on the number line.
questions.prompt_markup:
A freezer is at 2°C and cools 1.5°C each hour.
Solve 2 - 1.5t < -4 to find when it is colder than -4°C. Then graph the solution on the number line.
questions.drawing_answer: An open circle at 4 with an arrow or shading to the right
questions.grading_note: Grade both: t > 4 and the graph with an open circle at 4 shaded to the right.

questions.skill: Graph the solution set of an inequality and interpret it in context
questions.prompt: Tickets cost $6 each. Jo has $40 and must keep at least $10, so 6t ≤ 30. The graph shows the solution as whole numbers. Which description fits the graph?
questions.prompt_markup:
Tickets cost $6 each. Jo has $40 and must keep at least $10, so 6t ≤ 30. The graph shows the solution as whole numbers.
Which description fits the graph?

choices.text: Jo can buy any number of tickets greater than 5.

figure.description: Horizontal number line from 0 to 8, tick marks every 1. Points: a point at 0, a point at 1, a point at 2, a point at 3, a point at 4, a point at 5.

questions.skill: Graph the solution set of an inequality and interpret it in context
questions.response: draw on the figure and write an answer
questions.prompt: A club has $30 and earns $5 for each ticket it sells. It needs more than $230. Solve 5t + 30 > 230. Then graph the possible numbers of tickets (whole numbers) on the number line.
questions.prompt_markup:
A club has $30 and earns $5 for each ticket it sells. It needs more than $230.
Solve 5t + 30 > 230. Then graph the possible numbers of tickets (whole numbers) on the number line.
questions.correct_answer: t > 40: the club must sell at least 41 tickets.
questions.drawing_answer: Dots at the whole numbers 41, 42, 43, ... to the end of the line, with an arrow or "..." to show the pattern continues; no dot at 40
questions.grading_note: Grade both: the solution with the context (at least 41 tickets), and the graph of whole numbers greater than 40.

figure.description: Horizontal number line from 30 to 50, tick marks every 1. Nothing is marked; the student draws on it.

questions.skill: Find the solution of a system of equations from its graph
questions.prompt: Two lines are graphed on the same grid. What does their point of intersection represent?
questions.prompt_markup:
Two lines are graphed on the same grid.
What does their point of intersection represent?
questions.correct_answer: The pair (x, y) that makes both equations true; the solution of the system.
